nodeData.note: How to grow sweet potato and cassava organically: clean vines and cuttings, spacing, organic nutrition, weevils, mosaic and brown streak, the mealybug biocontrol story, harvest and safe processing. Search words: viazi vitamu, muhogo, OFSP, manioc, yuca, CMD, CBSD, Cylas.

children.note: Two hardy root crops grown from stem cuttings, not seed. Both came from South America and are now food-security crops across East Africa.
A creeping vine of the morning-glory family with sweet storage roots. Only distantly related to Irish potato and not a yam at all. Swahili: viazi vitamu.

manas.q: Which plant family does sweet potato belong to?

children.note: A woody shrub of the spurge family grown for its starchy roots. More than 500 million people depend on it; it is the tropics' third-biggest source of carbohydrate. Swahili: muhogo.

manas.q: Roughly how many people depend on cassava?

children.note: Young sweet potato leaves are a nutritious green (about 20% protein in dry matter); vines are good dry-season fodder. Cassava leaves are eaten too, but only after proper cooking.
Orange flesh means beta-carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A. It is promoted in East Africa to fight vitamin A deficiency in children.

manas.q: Why is orange-fleshed sweet potato promoted for children?

children.note: Cassava can stay in the ground for months and survive drought by dropping leaves, so families plant it as insurance against a failed season.
Both like warmth and good drainage. Neither stands waterlogging; both give something on poor soil, but yield follows organic matter.
Grows from sea level to about 3,000 m near the equator; best above 25 °C, slowed below 12 °C or above 35 °C; 600–1,600 mm of well-spread rain.
Dry weather helps roots form and bulk, but drought right after planting or at root initiation cuts yield badly.

manas.q: When is drought most harmful to sweet potato?

children.note: Up to about 1,500 m near the equator, 20–30 °C, best with 1,000–1,500 mm; once established it survives on far less rain. It needs sun and free drainage.
Best on fertile sandy loams, pH about 5.5–7.5; poor on heavy clays, stony ground, saline soils or pH above 8. Very rich soil makes leaves instead of roots.

manas.q: Why can very fertile soil reduce cassava root yield?

children.note: Sweet potato ridges are about 30–45 cm high and 90–120 cm apart, run along the contour on slopes. Cassava goes on mounds or ridges where rain exceeds about 1,200 mm or land waterlogs.
The single biggest organic lever. Both crops pass viruses and pests to the next field through cuttings, so what you plant decides what you harvest.
The top 20–40 cm of the vine (5–8 nodes) roots fastest and is least likely to carry weevils or disease. Bury one-third to two-thirds, at least 2–3 nodes.

manas.q: Which part of the sweet potato vine makes the best cutting, and why?

children.note: Strip lower leaves, wrap bundles in a wet sack and keep them in shade; 1–2 days in humid storage can help rooting, longer weakens them.
Plant clean vines at about 15 × 20 cm in a separate plot; new cuttings are ready after about 45 days. Single-node cuttings in a humus-rich seedbed multiply vines fast.
Repeated vine propagation builds up viruses, often without obvious signs. Clean, heat-treated or tissue-culture material can yield 20–200% more for a few seasons.

manas.q: Why do old sweet potato varieties seem to yield less over time?

children.note: 20–30 cm long, 20–25 mm thick, 5–8 nodes, from the middle brown part of 8–14-month-old healthy stems. Plant within a couple of days, never upside down.

manas.q: What size should a cassava cutting be?

children.note: Mix equal volumes of boiling and cold water and dip lightly infested cassava cuttings for 5–10 minutes just before planting, to kill mites and mealybugs.

manas.q: How do you make the hot-water dip for cassava cuttings?

children.note: Get virus-free or tissue-culture cassava and sweet potato from KALRO and other national research stations, then keep your own clean multiplication plot.
Plant at the start of the rains (or any time where there is no hard dry season). Spacing sets root size.
Ridges 90–120 cm apart with 20–30 cm between cuttings (3–5 per metre). Closer spacing gives more but smaller roots; wider gives larger roots.
Two cuttings per mound show little benefit; single cuttings tend to give more large roots.
Sole crop at 1 × 1 m = 10,000 cuttings per hectare (about 4,000 per acre). Leave more room when intercropping.

manas.q: How many cassava cuttings are needed per acre at 1 × 1 m?

children.note: In dry soil plant at an angle with most of the stem buried; vertical suits sandy soils; flat planting gives shallow roots that rodents find.
Weed cassava every 3–4 weeks until 2–3 months, when the canopy closes. Pulled weeds can be left as mulch.
Cassava grows on poor soil but removes a lot when yields are high. Sweet potato needs organic matter more than nitrogen.
Compost and manure help the soil hold water, which protects sweet potato from drought and keeps soil from cracking — cracks let weevils in.
Phosphorus drives root growth; potassium fills roots. Use compost or manure at land preparation, rock phosphate for P and wood ash for K.

manas.q: Which two organic inputs supply cassava's P and K?

children.note: P shortage: stunting with purple leaves. K shortage: dark leaves turning pale, then brown dry tips and 'burnt' edges.

manas.q: What leaf colour signals phosphorus shortage in cassava?

children.note: Sow a row of canavalia or crotalaria between cassava rows after planting, and plough residues in after harvest; cowpea or groundnut also cut runoff.
Kilifi farmers mix fresh Lantana leaves into sweet potato mounds, reporting fewer weevils and better roots. A farmer experience, not a trial result.
Mulch keeps soil moist and even-temperatured, stops crusting and cracking, and shelters natural enemies.
Rock phosphate, ash and manure in depth.
Reading leaves for N, P, K and more.
Weevils and the virus complex are the two big threats. Both are managed by clean vines, rotation and closing soil cracks.
Cylas puncticollis, C. brunneus and C. formicarius. Larvae tunnel vines and roots; damaged roots rot, smell and turn bitter even with light damage.

manas.q: Why are even lightly weevil-damaged roots unfit to eat?

children.note: Weevils cannot dig. They find roots through cracks in drying soil, so dry seasons and late harvests mean more damage.
Plant vine tips, plant deep, hill up and mulch or irrigate to close cracks, rotate with cereals, remove wild Ipomoea weeds, harvest on time.
Roots with egg holes infest clean roots beside them in store. Sort them out at harvest.
A combination of two viruses (feathery mottle, spread by aphids, and chlorotic stunt, spread by whiteflies) causes severe stunting and small, distorted leaves.

manas.q: Which two viruses combine to cause sweet potato virus disease?

children.note: Clean vines, resistant varieties, pulling out sick plants, keeping new plots away from old ones, and controlling aphids and whiteflies.
Slow, many-legged 'Mombasa train' that gathers in moist, organic-rich soil and nibbles roots. Usually minor.
How plant viruses spread and are managed.
Two viruses and two pests from South America cause most losses. The cassava story is also the great success of biological control.
Spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings: yellow-green mosaic patches, distorted small leaves, stunting. A 1920s outbreak caused famine; a more severe form arose in Uganda in the late 1980s.

manas.q: How does cassava mosaic disease spread?

children.note: Inspect weekly for the first 2–3 months and pull out sick plants — worth it only while fewer than about 5% are infected, and best done by a whole village.

manas.q: When is roguing worth doing for cassava mosaic?

children.note: Caused by two ipomoviruses (CBSV and UCBSV). Leaves may look nearly normal while roots rot with brown streaks — a hidden thief. Serious on the Kenyan coast and in Uganda.

manas.q: Why is brown streak called a 'hidden' disease?

children.note: Plant only clean cuttings, use tolerant varieties, uproot diseased plants, and check roots of a few plants before taking cuttings.
Tiny mites cause yellow pinprick spots and, in bad dry seasons, a bare 'candle-stick' shoot tip; root losses of 20–80%. Don't confuse with mosaic.
Predatory mites brought from South America (mainly Typhlodromalus aripo) now keep green mite down in much of Africa. Intercropping with pigeon pea also helps.
A pink, waxy mealybug that causes stunted 'bunchy tops' in the dry season; losses up to 80%. Weak plants on poor sandy soils suffer most.

manas.q: What symptom does cassava mealybug cause at the shoot tip?

children.note: The parasitic wasp Anagyrus lopezi, released across Africa from the 1980s, brought the mealybug under control; Hans Rudolf Herren received the 1995 World Food Prize.

manas.q: Which natural enemy brought cassava mealybug under control in Africa?

children.note: Avoid insecticide drift from neighbouring fields; it kills the natural enemies that keep cassava pests down.
Parasitoids and predators in depth.
Sweet potato should be harvested early to escape weevils; cassava spoils within days of harvest. Bitter cassava must be processed before eating.
Piecemeal harvesting is common for home use; harvest within about 4 months to limit weevil damage. Dig carefully to avoid wounds.
Usually 9–12 months after planting (early types about 6). Late harvest makes roots woody. Typical yields 7.5–10 t/ha; 25 t/ha or more with good care.

manas.q: How long after planting is cassava usually harvested?

children.note: Fresh roots blacken and go off within 2–3 days. Leave them in the ground until needed, or peel, chop and sun-dry chips (about 3 kg fresh makes 1 kg chips).

manas.q: About how much fresh cassava makes 1 kg of dry chips?

children.note: All cassava contains cyanide-releasing compounds; bitter types have far more (up to about 1,000 mg/kg vs 20 in sweet types), and drought raises levels.

manas.q: Why must bitter cassava be processed before eating?

children.note: Soaking, fermenting, grating and drying or cooking release the cyanide. Brief soaking alone is not enough. Poor processing in famine times causes konzo.
Both crops are spreading again in dry counties and in nutrition programmes. Choose varieties with KALRO and buy clean planting material.
Both are household food-security crops grown on the coast, in western and in drier parts of Kenya. Check which suits your zone with your county extension office.
Kenyan cassava lines such as KME 2 come through KALRO. Ask KALRO or your county office for current cassava and orange-fleshed sweet potato varieties; on the coast ask for brown-streak tolerance.
Taking cuttings from sick or unknown plants is how mosaic, brown streak and weevils travel. Clean material first, always.

children.topic: Mistake: leaving sweet potato too long
children.note: Roots left in cracked, dry soil after maturity are where weevil losses climb.
Sweet potato reached Polynesia before Europeans did and later became Japan's famine crop; cassava now spans Africa, Asia and Latin America.
